subject: Air-gapped private deployment: inventory, maintenance windows & SLA next steps
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Shah <samir@genomex.com>, Angela Pierce <angela.procure@genomex.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 02 Aug 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Air-gapped private deployment: inventory, maintenance windows & SLA next steps

Hi Samir / Angela — thanks again for the deep-dive earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before Ben and Lauren loop in Ops for sizing and procurement: 

Call highlights:
- Genomex confirmed intent to run Redwood in an air-gapped on-prem setup (private appliance + customer-managed network).
- Primary use case: internal research assistant for genomic analysis, occasional batch inference (peak: 48 concurrent sessions/day).
- Security asks: quarterly firmware/patch schedule, audit logs retention 3 years, and offline upgrade process for classification model updates.

Open questions we agreed to follow up on:
1) Hardware inventory: we need a full server/rack inventory (make/model, CPU, GPU type, RAM, network cards) to validate compatibility with our appliance and to size the Dedicated bundle. Please attach a spreadsheet if possible.
2) Maintenance windows: what day/time windows are available for applying firmware/OS updates? Are there blackout periods for production research runs?
3) Upgrade cadence: how does Genomex want to receive model and runtime updates in an air-gapped environment? Options: (A) offline package + signed artifact (our typical flow), (B) swap-in USB recovery image, (C) on-site technician-assisted upgrade.
4) On-call escalation: primary and secondary contacts and expected response SLA for P1/P2 incidents.

Attachments: I included a blank site_inventory.xlsx for your convenience and a proposed_network_diagram.pdf with the minimal firewall/NAT configuration we typically require.

Next steps (proposed):
- Action (Genomex): Fill site_inventory.xlsx and return by EOD 8/6 so we can run a compatibility check.
- Action (Redwood): Ben to produce a preliminary bill-of-materials and compatibility notes after inventory review (target 8/9).
- Action (Redwood): Lauren to draft an ops SLA and maintenance cadence proposal for review (target 8/9).

If that timeline looks good, I’ll flag a follow-up for 8/10 to review findings and agree on procurement items.

Thanks — Rachel

--
Rachel Kim | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192
Redwood Inference — production-grade inference across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments
[Attachment: site_inventory.xlsx (xlsx, 14KB)]
[Attachment: proposed_network_diagram.pdf (pdf, 220KB)]

From: Samir Shah <samir@genomex.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Angela Pierce <angela.procure@genomex.com>
Cc: IT Ops <itops@genomex.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Aug 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Air-gapped private deployment: inventory, maintenance windows & SLA next steps

Rachel — thanks for the summary and helpful templates. Quick answers from our end: 

1) Inventory: attaching an initial export from our asset manager. It’s incomplete (missing NIC firmware revisions) but should be enough for a first pass. We’ll try to populate the blanks by Friday.
2) Maintenance windows: weekly maintenance can run Sat 02:00–06:00 PT. We have monthly long-maintenance 3rd Sat 00:00–08:00 PT. Blackout: none currently scheduled but Q4 has heavy runs, will call that out in the completed inventory.
3) Upgrade cadence: we prefer option (A) offline package with signed artifacts. We want the ability to opt into scheduled upgrades rather than forced pushes.
4) On-call: IT Ops will be primary. I put their contact in cc — please include them on any runbook drafts.

Attaching: gen_inventory_initial.xlsx (export), network_note.txt (short note on NAT/firewall).

—Samir

[Attachment: gen_inventory_initial.xlsx (xlsx, 47KB)]
[Attachment: network_note.txt (txt, 2KB)]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 05 Aug 2027 11:35:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: compatibility review and BOM ask (Genomex DX-7831)

Rachel / Lauren — I reviewed Samir’s initial inventory. Notes:
- Several servers list A100S/80GB variants which are ideal; two racks show mixed older GPUs (V100/T4) that may require a secondary plan (runtime fallback with quantized model or reduced concurrency).
- Network: public NAT + restricted egress. We should confirm whether we can receive signed offline artifacts via a removable media process or whether a controlled egress host is permitted for a secure pull.

I’ll draft a short compatibility table and provisional BOM (three possible skus: full-capacity, mixed-fleet, conservative-quantized) — will share by Monday 8/9. Lauren, can you start an ops SLA draft covering: patch cadence (quarterly), audit log retention, incident routing, and a proposed P1/P2 response window? Put it in the shared drive link Rachel listed.

Ben

--
Ben Carter | Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 (650) 555-0123

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Shah <samir@genomex.com>, Angela Pierce <angela.procure@genomex.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, IT Ops <itops@genomex.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Aug 2027 16:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Air-gapped private deployment: inventory, maintenance windows & SLA next steps — actions confirmed

Hi all — thanks for the quick turns. Finalizing commitments below so procurement and CloudSec have a single source of truth: 

Confirmed decisions:
- Genomex prefers air-gapped private appliance with offline signed artifacts for model/runtime updates (option A).
- Maintenance window accepted: weekly Sat 02:00–06:00 PT; monthly long-maintenance 3rd Sat 00:00–08:00 PT.
- Inventory: Samir will return a completed spreadsheet with NIC firmware versions and rack elevations by EOD 8/13.
- SLA: Redwood to provide a draft (quarterly patch cadence, 3-year audit log retention, P1 response target: 2 hours to acknowledge; P2: 4 hours). Lauren will upload draft by 8/9 and Ben will annotate compatibility items in the BOM.

Immediate next steps (owners & dates):
- Genomex (Samir): Complete inventory and return 8/13.
- Redwood (Ben): BOM + compatibility table by 8/09 (uploaded to Drive).
- Redwood (Lauren): Ops SLA draft uploaded 8/09 for review.
- Rachel: Schedule sync on 8/16 at 10:00 AM PT to review final BOM and procurement path. Calendar invite to follow.

Questions for Genomex before the 8/16 sync:
- Will the customer provide a secure USB handoff process or a dedicated egress host for artifact pulls? If USB, please confirm chain-of-custody process.
- Any additional compliance requirements (FedRAMP, HIPAA) beyond SOC2 we should prepare for?

Thanks — looking forward to the next steps.

Rachel

--
Rachel Kim | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192
